pr_body:
Currently, these two flags were implied by dissect_loop_device(), but that's not right, because this means systemd-gpt-auto-generator will dissect the root block device with these flags set and that's not desirable: the generator should not cause the partition devices to be created (we don't intend to use them right-away after all, but expect udev to find/probe them first, and then mount them though .mount units). And there's no point in opening the partition devices, since we do not intend to mount them via fds either.

Hence, rework this: instead of implying the flags, specify them explicitly.

While we are at it, let's also rename the flags to make them more descriptive:

DISSECT_IMAGE_MANAGE_PARTITION_DEVICES becomes
DISSECT_IMAGE_ADD_PARTITION_DEVICES, since that's really all this does: add the partition devices via BLKPG.

DISSECT_IMAGE_OPEN_PARTITION_DEVICES becomes
DISSECT_IMAGE_PIN_PARTITION_DEVICES, since we not only open the devices, but keep the devices open continously (i.e. we "pin" them).

Also, drop the DISSECT_IMAGE_BLOCK_DEVICE combination flag, since it is misleading, i.e. it suggests it was appropriate to specify on all dissected blocking devices, but that's precisely not the case, see the systemd-gpt-auto-generator case. My guess is that the confusion around this was actually the cause for this bug we are addressing here.

Fixes: #25528
pr_comments: CI failures seem unrelated (sleep time out in TEST-17-UDEV and the usual integrity test timeout)

issue_context.title: systemd-gpt-auto-generator shouldn't cause creations of partitions
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252

### Used distribution

Fedora Rawhide

### Linux kernel version used

6.1.0-0.rc6.46.fc38.x86_64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-gpt-auto-generator

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

systemd-gpt-auto-generator should only scan the root block device and create respective mount units based on the content of GPT parition table.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

It seems that generator causes scan of the partition table by the kernel and creation of respective partition devices. This is done in `block_device_add_partition()` and requires `sys_admin` capability which is not granted by the SELinux on Fedora. AVC is message is logged and error is ignored on the generator side. My main issue is that rescan of the partition table needs to happen anyway at later point because systemd-udevd is not running when the generator is executed during boot and probing partitions at such early time seems wasteful and unnecessary.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

```strace -e ioctl /usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/systemd-gpt-auto-generator /tmp /tmp /tmp 2>&1 | grep BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

```sh
ioctl(4, BLKPG, {op=BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION, flags=0, datalen=152, data={start=1048576, length=1048576, pno=1, devname="/dev/vda1", volname=""}}) = -1 EBUSY (Device or resource busy)
ioctl(4, BLKPG, {op=BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION, flags=0, datalen=152, data={start=2097152, length=21472722432, pno=2, devname="/dev/vda2", volname=""}}) = -1 EBUSY (Device or resource busy)
```
comments: We discussed this with @msekletar yesterday. The conclusion was that this is OK and expected. https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/1b010ae7c96d953f11a9925d4c5aef29befc86d1 added a call to BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION to work around a problem with the kernel asynchronously and unpredictably detecting partitions on its own. Instead of waiting for the kernel to read the partition table and create device notices for the partitions, we tell the kernel to "add" a partition. The partition already exists on disk, so the only change is in the volatile state in the kernel. There are no plans to change this, because this approach is more robust than the other approaches that were tried previously and suffered from various race conditions.
Ah, found it. This gets ORed in implicitly in `dissect_loop_device()` which is used in enumerate_partitions() in systemd-gpt-auto-generator. And it really should not. Will prep fix.
@msekletar can you check if #25580 fixes the issue for you?
Is this bug related to this one -> https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2083900
@poettering JFYI, the original SELinux issue is gone. Thanks!

review_comments: Does it make sense to have this as a separate flag? At least in this PR, you either specify none of these two flags or both of them, so why have two flags instead of one?

well, the previous version of the code added a combined enum that merged the two flags under one name. I dropped that mostly because I couldn't find a clear name for it htat was better than the separate flags. 

The two operations of the two flags are really different I think. While they usually are used in combination I would still keep them seperate because they are so different.

I mean, I could even see a real-life usecase for this. For example, I think we probably should add "systemctl-dissect --attach" which validates a DDI and synchronously attaches a la "losetup -P", but doesn't actually mount it. Could be useful of you then want to mount it via mount units (potentially even dynamic automount units via systemd-mount) or via udisks or so. In that case we want the ADD but not the PIN.
